title: Changing the Keel Artifact runs through the Root Edit Primitive, separate from Keel's other governance information
content:
A.6.1.1.3.3.1 is titled "Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive" and defines itself by exclusion: it holds "Keel governance information that is unrelated to the use of the Root Edit Primitive," while "the governance process for updating the Keel Artifact is specified in the Root Edit Primitive above at A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2."

The split separates two categories that are easy to conflate. Amending the Artifact changes the rules Keel operates under; ordinary governance information (forum venue, emergency protocols, accords) operates *within* those rules. Only the first is a Primitive.

Routing self-amendment through a Primitive matters because Primitives carry the machinery described elsewhere in the Artifact — a defined Invocation process, recorded outcomes, and archived failures. An Agent's power to rewrite its own mandate is the most consequential power it has, so placing it inside that machinery means every attempted change leaves a durable record, including changes that fail.

The naming convention is also telling: the residual branch is defined negatively, by what it is *not*. Root Edit is the reference point around which the rest of Keel's governance documentation is arranged, which signals that self-amendment is treated as the primary governance concern rather than one item among many.
description: The Artifact splits governance that alters the document itself from governance that merely operates within it, keeping self-amendment inside a Primitive with defined process.
